hypothesis: Adding an optional bounded minimum raw-relevance gate to exact-token change search will let hosts remove partial-match noise without conflating lexical relevance with ranking confidence or answer utility.
heldOutChecks: default search behavior remains unchanged when the gate is omitted
a minimum raw relevance of 1 returns only the full raw-retrieval-ranking match
the gate is applied to raw relevance before result limiting and preserves deterministic order
project and kind filters intersect with the raw-relevance gate
CLI and MCP return equivalent gated results and reject out-of-range or hostile values
a gated no-match query returns an empty result set without confidence, utility or semantic inference

memoryDecision.exactBaseline: unweighted exact-token overlap with optional project and kind filters
memoryDecision.candidate: optional threshold over the already exposed raw token-overlap fraction
memoryDecision.ruvectorWasm: defer until at least 100 sanitized provenance records support leakage-free exact, vector and fused comparisons
memoryDecision.gnn: reject unless a held-out graph task demonstrates at least ten percentage points of task-success gain over exact retrieval and a shuffled-graph control

forecast.prediction: Within 60 days, agent-memory retrieval interfaces will increasingly expose a configurable retrieval-relevance gate that is explicitly separate from answer confidence, downstream ranking and value-of-information decisions.
forecast.falsifiableCriterion: By 2026-11-18, at least two primary agent-memory implementations or interoperability specifications newly document a raw retrieval threshold or risk-coverage control separately from answer confidence or downstream ranking.
